text:
elaine: quick flag — saw ~18 inbound leads this afternoon that went to the same SDR (alex) despite rotation enabled. SLA is 10m to owner; some hits 45m. anyone know if rotation broke?

tom: ugh. that's the rotation service. on it. can you drop a couple lead ids and the time range?

elaine: ids: 88541, 88567, 88590. they were created between 13:12-13:40 UTC. HubSpot shows Owner set to Alex but our rotation logs show same hash for all.

devon: looking at rotation code — we recently reverted deterministic hashing change (PR #412) and left the fallback to index 0 when hashing fails. if active_reps list was empty momentarily due to cache invalidation, hash -> null -> index 0 -> same rep.

rachael: that matches salesops alerts — we had a short cache flush at 13:10 during config rollout. could be the timing.

salesops-bot: Deploy: hs-workflows/inbound-fallback -> staging by @rachael

elaine: temporary mitigation: can we add a HS workflow that says: if Owner empty OR Owner == "alex" && lead.source="inbound" && assign_count_recent>3 -> route to `inbound-rotation-fallback` queue, notify #sales-ops?

devon: yes. suggested short-term workflow: ```if HubSpot Owner is unknown OR HubSpot Owner equals "alex" AND Lead created < 30m ago -> Set Owner = round_robin(inbound-active)```. we'll also add a guard so we never write over a manually set owner.

qa: i'll run a smoke test against staging: create 10 leads with created_at within 1m, verify assignment distribution. steps: 1) create leads via HS API 2) tail rotation-service logs 3) check HS owner property.

devon: for the permanent fix: 1) avoid defaulting to index 0 when reps list empty — instead retry fetching reps with exponential backoff up to 5s, 2) emit metric rotation.error and rotation.assign_owner with rep_id tag, 3) add e2e test that simulates cache eviction. will open a PR.

rachael: for SLA governance: can we add a rule in our alerts: if median TTA > 8m or >5 leads unassigned >15m in 30m window -> page sales-ops lead pager and post summary to #lead-routing.

tom: also adding telemetry to the lead assignment path helps root cause postmortem: log cause=(cache_miss|hash_fail|api_error|manual) and include lead_id. query for audit: ```SELECT lead_id, created_at, assigned_at, assigned_by, assignment_cause FROM lead_assignments WHERE created_at > now()- interval 1 day ORDER BY created_at DESC;```

salesops-bot: Deploy complete: hs-workflows/inbound-fallback -> production (success)

elaine: staging smoke looked good. pushed the workflow to prod. watch list: 88541,88567,88590

qa: smoke results: distribution across 5 reps, no single-rep lock. posting CSV to #analytics. median tta prefix (last 24h) = 12m, post-patch 45m window = 5m. 95th dropped from 78m -> 18m.

devon: opened PR #427 with backoff + metrics + unit tests. added integration test to simulate empty rep list and verify retry.

rachael: i'll update comms: short note to sales ops + quick FAQ for SDRs: "you might see routing flaps around 13:10-13:45 UTC — if you get >5 duplicate leads, escalate to sales-ops@redwood.com".

tom: next steps: merge PR, run canary for 1 hour, monitor rotation.error > 0 or any single-rep >= 40% of inbound for the hour -> rollback. assign @devon to the ticket, @rachael to comms.

elaine: thanks team. closing loop: workaround applied, permanent fix in PR, monitoring thresholds added. keep posting any stray lead ids here. :rocket:
